The build already reads strongly as the tithe barn — cobblestone shell, stone_brick plinth, gabled plank roof, the cobblestone gable end with apex vent, and the punched bay rhythm with wagon doors all land. The conformance gate fully passes.

issues.issue: Entire roof painted dark_oak_planks (the pack's roof.trim accent) instead of roof.field spruce_planks; reads too dark/cool versus the concept's warm-brown plank roof and misuses the field/trim vocabulary split.
Concept shows prominent full-height stone_brick pilaster strips separating each cobblestone bay; my long walls read as mostly plain cobblestone with only lintel dressing.
Concept's gable vent slit is a touch more pronounced; mine is faint but present.

rounds.rationale: Switch the roof field from the dark_oak trim block to the pack's designated roof.field spruce_planks, matching the concept's warm-brown plank roof and restoring the intended field/trim vocabulary; all conformance checks remain satisfied.

stone gable triangle with apex slit window matches the concept well

rounds.rationale: The concept's defining facade feature is two wooden wagon doors; this swaps the first stone-filled door bay to oak_planks (door.wagon), staying in-pack and gate-safe, with the second door to follow next round.

issues.issue: concept fills these full-height bays with warm wooden wagon doors (oak_planks/door.wagon); my build leaves them as dark empty holes

silhouette, dominant dark gable roof, stone plinth, and cobblestone gable triangle with apex slit all match the concept well

rounds.rationale: The mass and roof read as the concept, but the shell's prime divergence — the concept's doored bays and stone-brick pilaster rhythm — can't be added cleanly with adjust-params or surface paint (no air-fill op), so I re-recognize the shell against the concept to re-derive those openings/doors; rollback protects conformance if it regresses.

Concept gable triangle is cobblestone wall carried up with a single high slit; mine is close but the raking stone-brick edge is faint.

rounds.rationale: Fill the first door bay (the +z wall opening at x15-17, y0-4) with oak_planks (door.wagon) so it reads as a closed wooden wagon door — the barn's signature feature, currently a dark void. This paints a defined plane region, keeps the palette in-pack, and improves watertightness; the second door bay is the natural follow-up next round.

the raking roof edge lacks the stepped stone_brick verge the concept shows along the gable; mass and apex otherwise match

rounds.rationale: Fill the left wagon-door bay with a proven in-pack wood block (dark_oak_planks) so the empty void reads as the concept's wagon door; this fixes last round's regression by swapping oak_planks (door-only, broke palette-in-pack) for dark_oak_planks, which is already the roof field and passes the palette gate. Single-bay paint held symmetry last round, so all six checks should survive; the mirror bay at x30 is the round-6 follow-up.
